name: TinaCMS
title: Mica vs. TinaCMS
summary: TinaCMS offers visual click-to-edit, a hosted service and an editorial workflow with pull requests. It keeps an index of your content in a database. Mica has none, and it has an MCP server for AI agents.

chooseMica.text: You want AI agents to edit your content: Mica has an MCP server built in. TinaCMS lists one as Coming Soon.
You use Astro and want click to edit on the real page without code in each template. Mica needs one integration, `micaPreview()`, and no change to the templates.
You have many large photos or files, which would bloat your Git repository. Mica keeps them out of the normal history, with Git LFS.
Your entries link to data that lives elsewhere: product data, place names, regions or codes. Mica uses thousands of items from a JSON or CSV file of your website, and never edits them.
You do not want a database or an index for your content.
You want to run the editor yourself in one container, behind any OpenID Connect provider.
Your content is on a Git host other than GitHub.
You want Astro to read your content through Content Collections, with types.
An editor should publish several changes as one commit, with a summary.
You need a map to pick places, and the page should show the same view: Mica stores the zoom with the place.

chooseOther.text: Editors should see the page change as they type, in real time in React, and click on the page to edit it. TinaCMS does this, also in Astro.
You want a hosted service (TinaCloud) with plans and support.
You want search over your content, through TinaCloud.
You want MDX components in your content.
You want an editorial workflow with draft pull requests (Business plan and up).

facts.value: Yes. GitHub only, with TinaCloud and with the self-hosted provider. Custom providers are possible.
The local dev server works without the cloud. Editing in production needs TinaCloud, or a self-hosted backend: a backend function, a database adapter, a Git provider and an auth provider.
Yes. The Data Layer indexes your content. TinaCloud hosts it. Self-hosted needs MongoDB or Redis/Vercel KV.
Apache-2.0. The Data Layer packages have a separate licence. Free for 2 users. Team $24 a month for each project. Team Plus $41. Business $249. Enterprise on request.
Official @tinacms/astro. Astro is the default starter. Content comes through a generated GraphQL client, not Content Collections. It needs an SSR adapter.
TinaCloud: GitHub or email. SSO on Enterprise. Self-hosted: Auth.js, Clerk, TinaCloud or custom. OIDC is not documented.
Each save is a commit. The Editorial Workflow (Business and up) uses a branch and a draft pull request. No batch publish.

Yes. The site and the editor side by side, in real time in React (useTina). A click on an element opens its form. On Astro, the site needs the tina() integration, requestWithMetadata() loaders, an island registry and route, TinaIsland and tinaField() in components, and SSR or islands. Each page is wired by hand.
Not supported (Git LFS keeps large files out of the normal history). The documentation names limits of the GitHub API.
Not documented. localContentPath points local development to a separate content repository.
Not documented. The reference field links to collections. Large collections can time out.
Documented patterns, by directory or by field. No locale switcher.
TinaCloud has Admin and Editor. More roles on paid plans. Review is the Editorial Workflow with pull requests (Business).
An MCP server and AI features are listed as Coming Soon.
